title: NYC Daily Digest
text:
Good morning, Matthew ☕
Thursday, September 17, 2026

🌤️ Weather
NYC today: mild and pleasant. High around 79°, low near 67°, mostly dry with just a small chance of a passing shower. What to wear: light layers — a t-shirt works midday, but grab a light jacket for the evening.

🗞️ Headlines
• The Fed raised rates 25 bps to 3.75%–4% — its first hike since 2023 — citing still-elevated inflation, and hinted at possibly one more before year-end.
• Rep. Thomas Massie moved to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on eight counts; House GOP leaders recessed to sidestep a pre-midterm vote, with Speaker Johnson calling it a "publicity stunt."
• A bipartisan group in Congress is pushing new national rules to curb partisan gerrymandering.
• A new national poll found nearly 60% of likely voters say the economy isn't working for their families, with care costs, wages, and paid leave topping their asks.
• Abroad: India summoned Pakistan's envoy after a naval collision in the Arabian Sea it called "unacceptable and unprofessional."

🚇 Getting around
Nothing major systemwide today. Heads-up for later: starting Friday night (9/18), Church Av-bound G trains skip 4 Av–9 St through Monday morning.

🎉 NYC today
• The Feast of San Gennaro kicks off in Little Italy (runs through 9/27) — cannoli, processions, and street food.
• Baseball: Mets host the Phillies at Citi Field tonight.
• Foodie bonus: "The Most Legendary Lunch Break" pop-up has award-winning chefs cooking gourmet lunches inside five Manhattan bodegas today.

💡 Nugget
That Fed hike is the first rate increase in three years — if you've got a savings account or CDs, high-yield rates just got a little more interesting; if you're eyeing a loan or mortgage, borrowing costs are creeping up, so timing matters.

Sources: AccuWeather, CNBC, NPR, MTA, Time Out NY, Euronews
